title: Help Emily Beat Leukemia
description: Emily, 21, is fighting high-risk acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). She urgently needs an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant to survive.

story.intro: Emily is a 21-year-old pre-med student at Boston University who was diagnosed with high-risk Philadelphia chromosome-positive Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (Ph+ ALL). She urgently needs an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant to have a chance at long-term survival. While insurance covers part of the treatment, the out-of-pocket costs, uncovered therapies, and loss of income for her family are devastating.

sections.title: The Diagnosis
sections.content:
It all started in January 2026, when Emily began experiencing intense weakness, petechiae on her legs, and frequent febrile episodes. On January 20th, after a blood panel showed pancytopenia and suspicious blast cells, she was rushed to the Hematology Department at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute in Boston.

Bone marrow biopsy and molecular analysis confirmed the diagnosis: B-cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (B-ALL), with the BCR-ABL1 fusion gene (Philadelphia chromosome positive). This is an aggressive form of leukemia that requires intensive therapy and transplant for long-term survival.

sections.title: The Treatment Protocol
sections.content:
Emily immediately began induction therapy with the HyperCVAD protocol combined with a tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI — Dasatinib) due to her Ph+ status. After two cycles of chemotherapy, she has achieved complete hematologic remission and minimal residual disease (MRD) is now measured at levels < 0.01%.

Her doctors recommend an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant from a matched donor to consolidate the remission. Her younger sister, Kate, has been found to be a perfect HLA match (10/10 compatibility) and has already agreed to be the donor.

sections.title: Why We Need Your Help
sections.content: We want to be completely transparent. Much of Emily's standard treatment is covered by her family's health insurance through her father's employer plan. But even with insurance, the financial burden has been crushing — and several critical treatments are not covered at all.
coveredItems: Tyrosine kinase inhibitor (Dasatinib) for Ph+ status (specialty drug copay: $2,800/month)
Allogeneic stem cell transplant + donor workup (Kate)
notCoveredItems: Out-of-pocket maximum already reached ($16,400) — ongoing copays and coinsurance
MRD monitoring by NGS sequencing — not routinely covered, private labs only
Next-generation TKIs (ponatinib) if resistance develops — prior authorization delays averaging 45 days
Biologic therapies if relapse occurs (blinatumomab, inotuzumab) — insurance denials common for Ph+ ALL
Family relocation and living expenses in Boston during 6+ months post-transplant

items.text: Insurance out-of-pocket costs (deductibles, copays, coinsurance already incurred)
MRD monitoring by NGS and advanced molecular testing (private labs)
Access to next-generation TKIs and biologic therapies (if relapse/resistance)
Post-transplant complications and uncovered medical costs
Family relocation, housing, and living expenses in Boston (6+ months)
Reserve fund for unforeseen medical emergencies

quote.text: I wanted to become a doctor to help people. Now I'm the one in the hospital bed, and I understand how important it is when strangers show up for you. Every donation isn't just money — it's a chance to keep dreaming. I promise you, when I beat this, I will spend my life helping patients who are going through what I'm going through right now.
quote.author: Emily R.

updates.title: Positive news from molecular testing! 💪
updates.content: The latest RT-PCR results are encouraging — BCR-ABL levels are below 0.01%! Her doctors at Dana-Farber are very pleased with the treatment response. The transplant is scheduled for late June. Her sister Kate is already completing preliminary donor testing.

updates.title: We've passed 700 donors! 🙏
updates.content: We have no words to express our gratitude. Emily has completed the second cycle of chemotherapy and her doctors have confirmed complete hematologic remission. Every dollar brings us closer to the transplant.

updates.title: Update from the hospital
updates.content: Emily has completed the first cycle of chemotherapy at Dana-Farber. She had neutropenia after treatment, but she was smiling while reading your messages. The nurses brought her a small celebration in her room. Your response has moved us deeply.

updates.title: The campaign has launched
updates.content: With heavy hearts but also with hope, we're launching this appeal for help. After two months of intensive therapy, her doctors have confirmed that the transplant is the only option for long-term cure. Even with insurance, the financial toll on our family has been devastating. We believe in the power of community.
